title: 2026-08-31-horizon-labyrinth-and-team-synchronicity
customer_attendees: Full Team - company wide (see org list)
summary: Quarterly cross-functional all-hands focused on operational observability, model rollouts, private deployment readiness, and a preview of priority projects for Q4. Leadership discussed tradeoffs between latency/cost, rollout guardrails, and a new experiment to reduce tail latency with adaptive batching. Recap included hiring ask, compliance timeline, and follow-ups: share the observability roadmap doc, schedule team-specific breakouts, and run a pilot for the adaptive-batching config with two customers.

Adaptive batching experiment to improve 99th percentile latency

transcript:
[13:30] Avery (Host): Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a late monday — appreciate folks taking time. Quick check, audio ok?
[13:31] Multiple: yep, sounds good\/loud and clear
[13:31] Avery: Cool. We're calling this the "horizon labyrinth" sync — bit of theater, but we wanted to frame how different streams are converging: observability, model rollouts, and Private readiness. We'll do 30 minutes of updates, then 20 minutes for Q&A and breakouts.
[13:32] Marisol: Quick housekeeping — we pushed updated hiring numbers to the drive, pls review before the manager sync. Also wanted to flag an ops incident last week that influenced some of our latency targets.
[13:33] Dylan: Yeah, outage was brief but exposed tail behavior in preemptible pools. We have a mitigation plan but it does mean we need to re-evaluate burst policies for Dedicated.
[13:34] Ravi (SE): On the technical side, we've been experimenting with adaptive batching — basically change batch size based on observed request concurrency and prefix cache hits. Early internal benches show ~18% cost savings at 95th with neutral quality, but 99th latency varies.
[13:35] Avery: That's the tradeoff — we want lower token cost without regressing on latency SLO. We'll talk about guardrails for rolling those experiments to hosted customers.
[13:36] Speaker 4: quick question, is adaptive batching something we push as an automatic runtime change or opt-in per customer?
[13:36] Ravi: Good question. Our current idea is canary it first on Hosted non-critical tiers, with explicit opt-in for Dedicated until it's matured. For Private, customers must approve because of the auto-scaling implications.
[13:37] Marisol: So that means product needs a config toggles and an audit trail — compliance wants clear logs of any runtime decisions.
[13:37] Sana (Security, interjects): Yeah, audit logs are non-negotiable for Private deployments. We also need to map where KMS operations appear in logs for any fallback to on-prem keys.
[13:38] Avery: Noted — Sana please work with Ravi and Dylan to capture those log points.
[13:39] Q&A started:
[13:39] Speaker 5 (Engineering): On the Dedicated pools, can we have dynamic priority tiers? The question is how to avoid noisy neighbors when customers burst.
[13:39] Dylan: We're moving toward per-customer priority weights and a bucketed burst window. It won't eliminate contention but helps localize impact. Also plan to add a soft-fallback policy to route some requests to cheaper regions during sustained bursts.
[13:40] Avery: New routing policy will require clear cost/latency trade-off UI in console. Product team to design copy and analytics surfaces.
[13:41] Tomas (Finance): On cost attribution, we need token-level breakdowns for mid-market customers — they want to understand reranking vs generation costs. Can we get more granularity?
[13:41] Ravi: Yes, token-level attribution is on the roadmap. We're prototyping a sampling-based collector that tags tokens by route/model. We expect some overhead but it can be optional per workspace.
[13:42] Marisol: We'll prioritize this for mid-market templates; finance will share the list of accounts that need immediate support.
[13:43] Avery: Switching gears — Private readiness. Sana, where are we on SOC2 gaps and the on-prem packaging?
[13:43] Sana: The big items are enhanced audit retention, HSM/KMS integration docs, and network segregation tests. We've got a vendor for pen tests and initial gap analysis done — target is to close 60% by mid-September.
[13:44] Marisol: Ops note — our installer has a dependency issue with kernel X that surfaced on one customer lab. Dylan and infra are triaging with a patch expected this week.
[13:45] Ravi: From the model side, onboarding larger models into Private requires a quantization profile and compilation step. We've built automated profile recommendations but customers may still need manual tuning for latency-sensitive workloads.
[13:46] Speaker 6 (Product): For canaries and rollouts, we propose three tiers: internal-only, invited customers, and general availability. Rollback hooks must be plumbed into the control plane. Thoughts?
[13:46] Marisol: Agree. Also suggest adding a quality regression check against a golden prompt-set before broad rollout.
[13:47] Speaker 7 (ML Research): The golden set is great, but we need to keep it small and representative — avoid overfitting the eval to production noise.
[13:48] Avery: Ok let's formalize: golden set + smoke quality check + latency SLO check before moving tiers. Ravi, can you put together the automated pipeline?
[13:48] Ravi: Yep, target by next fortnight. Will include threshold config per model family.
[13:49] Audience question: How do we communicate failures to customers during rollouts?
[13:49] Avery: We'll have a standard status page incident flow plus per-customer outage notifications for Dedicated/Private. Also consider proactive fallback to a smaller-but-compatible model if the new variant underperforms.
[13:50] Marisol: We need to update runbooks and CSM templates.
[13:50] Tomas: Finance follow-up — what pricing levers do we have if customers want the new batching optimizations but we're still in canary?
[13:51] Avery: Could offer early-adopter credits or a pilot discount. We'll coordinate with growth on messaging.
[13:51] Sana: Quick flag on legal — for on-prem deployments we must ensure the contract language around data retention and KMS custody is explicit. Legal will push a template.
[13:52] Breakout scheduling note: Avery: We'll open breakout slots — engineering, security, and finance tracks. Please sign up.
[13:53] Final recap: Avery: To recap, observability roadmap will be shared, adaptive batching pilot planned, Private compliance checklist due, and hiring numbers updated. Marisol will lead hiring prioritization.
[13:54] Ravi: One more technical note — we're seeing noise in our 99th pct latency caused by cold KV cache misses; there's an idea to pre-warm for scheduled traffic windows. Will test with internal traffic first.
[13:55] Marisol: Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned and invites for breakouts follow.
[13:56] End of meeting.
